title: Individual Zones of Optimal Functioning: anxiety as facilitative within bounds and detrimental beyond a learner-specific optimal zone
description: The article adopts a multidimensional account of assessment anxiety in which moderate arousal can be facilitative while anxiety beyond an individual's optimal zone triggers threat responses (fight, flight, freeze, fawn) that impair working memory and undermine the validity of oral assessments. It states that "Models such as the Individual Zones of Optimal Functioning (IZOF) highlight that optimal anxiety levels vary considerably between learners, shaped by factors including trait anxiety, prior experiences and emotion regulation capacity". This frames the study's focus on anxiety that exceeds optimal arousal rather than anxiety as inherently harmful.
requirements: Assessment design decisions should be evaluated against individual differences in optimal arousal rather than a single anxiety threshold
constraints: The article notes the point at which anxiety becomes counterproductive is especially variable among learners who experience social anxiety or who are neurodivergent
target_learners: pre-university and higher-education students facing oral performance-based assessments, including socially anxious and neurodivergent learners
target_learning_goals: preserving valid demonstration of competence by keeping assessment anxiety within manageable, facilitative bounds
examples: The study distinguishes facilitative anxiety from excessive anxiety and targets the latter when interpreting AIvaluate's anxiety-reduction results
